item.title: 3. The Airplane
item.description: The Wright Brothers achieved the first powered, controlled flight in 1903, forever changing human mobility. Aviation shrank the world by enabling rapid international travel and global trade networks. It also transformed warfare, exploration, and disaster response. Modern globalization owes much to the airplane’s revolutionary impact.

item.title: MUST SEE: Here Are 10 Conservative Women Who Changed America…
item.description: 1. Margaret Thatcher (1925–2013) Margaret Thatcher, though British (Prime Minister 1979–1990), profoundly shaped American conservatism through her alliance with Ronald Reagan. Her policies of deregulation, free markets, anti-unionism, and staunch anti-communism inspired Reaganomics and the conservative revival in the U.S., shifting global and American discourse toward individualism and limited government.
